I’ve been anxious pretty much all the time for at least the last year and a half. It’s like my brain never shuts up—constantly running through worst‑case scenarios about work, money, my health, my family. I used to be pretty organized with projects, but now I struggle to keep track of versions, notes, and timelines because my mind drifts into “what if” spirals. It’s less that something around me distracts me and more that my own worrying thoughts pull me away from what I’m doing.

Physically I feel keyed up, like I’m running on nervous energy. Even when I’m sitting in the editing bay, I’m bouncing my leg or pacing during renders, almost like I’m propelled by the anxiety itself. I talk a lot in meetings too—rambling, overexplaining—because I’m nervous about being misunderstood or criticized. At night, the same worries keep looping and I can’t wind down.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
